B. Syllable 1
Understand the main errors of our age, which are noted in the Addresses
consistoriales, in the Encyclicals and in other apostolic Letters of N. SS. Pope Pius XII

S I. Pantheism, naturalism and absolute rationalism

2901 1. There is no divine being, supreme, most wise and most providential, distinct from this
university of things, and God is the same as nature, and therefore subject to change and, in
In reality, God is becoming in man and in the world, and everything is God and has the same
substance of God; and one and the same thing are God and the world and, therefore, the spirit and the
matter, necessity and freedom, true and false, good and evil, just and unjust
(26).

2902 2. All action of God on men and on the world must be denied (26).

2903 3. Human reason, without taking God into account, is the only arbiter of what
true and false, good and evil; It is a law of itself and by its natural forces it is enough
to seek the good of men and people (26).

2904 4. All the truths of religion derive from the native force of human reason; from there
that reason is the main norm, by which man can and must achieve knowledge
of truths of any kind (1, 17 and 26).

2905 5. Divine revelation is imperfect and, therefore, subject to continuous and indefinite progress,
in keeping with the progress of human reason (1 [cf. 1636] and 26).

2906 6. The faith of Christ is opposed to human reason; and divine revelation not only does not profit
for nothing, but harms the perfection of man (1 [cf. 1636] and 26).

2907 7. The prophecies and miracles exposed and narrated in the Sacred Letters are fictions of
poets; and the mysteries of the Christian faith, a set of philosophical investigations; and in the books
Both Testaments contain mythical inventions, and Jesus Christ himself is a fiction.
mythical (1 and 26).

S II. Moderate rationalism

2908 8. Since human reason is equated with religion itself, the sciences
Theological questions are to be treated in the same way as philosophical questions (18 [v. 1642]).

2909 9. All dogmas of the Christian religion are indiscriminately subject to corruption
natural, that is, of philosophy; and human reason, if only it is historically cultivated,
can arrive by its natural forces and principles to a true science of all dogmas,
even the most recondite ones, provided that these dogmas were proposed as an object to the
same reason (27 [cf. 1682] and 30).

2910 10. Since the philosopher is one thing and philosophy another, the former has the right and the duty to
submit to the authority that you have recognized as true; but philosophy neither can nor
he must submit to some authority (27 [v. 1673 and 1674] and 30).

2911 11. The Church must not only never rebuke philosophy, but must tolerate its
mistakes and let her correct herself (27 [v. 1675]).

2912 12. The Decrees of the Apostolic See and the Roman Congregations prevent free
progress of science (30 [v. 1679]).

2913 13. The method and principles with which the ancient scholastic doctors cultivated the
theology, they do not suit to the needs of our times and to the progress of science (30 [v.
1680]).

2914 14. Philosophy must be treated without taking into account supernatural revelation at all (30).
NB. Most of the errors of Antonio Gunther are linked to rationalism, who
They condemn in the letter to the Cardinal Archbishop of Cologne Eximiam tuam, dated June 15, 1875
(19 [cf. 1655]) and in the letter to the bishop of Breelau Dolore huud mediocri, dated April 90, 1860
(21).

$ III. Indifferentism, latitudinarianism

2915 15. Every man is free to embrace and profess the religion that, guided by the light of reason,
considered true (8 and 26).

2916 16. Men can find in the worship of any religion the path of
eternal salvation and achieving eternal salvation (1, 3 and 17).

2917 17. At least one must have well-founded hopes about the eternal salvation of all
those who are not in any way in the true Church of Christ (13 [v. 1646] and 28
[1677]).

2918 18. Protestantism is nothing other than a different form of the same true religion
Christian and in it, the same as in the Catholic Church, one can please God (5).

S IV. Socialism, communism, secret societies, biblical societies, clergy-liberal societies

These pestilential doctrines have been condemned many times and with the most serious words,
in the Encyclical letter Qui pluribus, dated December 9, 1846 (1); in the Quibus Address

2919 19. The Church is not a true and perfect society, completely free, nor does it enjoy its
own and constant rights conferred upon it by its divine Founder, but it is up to the

2921 21. The Church does not have the power to dogmatically define that the religion of the Church

2922 22. The obligation that totally binds Catholic teachers and writers is limited only to

2923 23. The Roman Pontiffs and the Ecumenical Councils crossed the limits of their

2924 24. The Church has no power to use force, nor any temporal power,
direct or indirect (9).

Its action on the entire Church is a doctrine that prevailed in the Middle Ages (9).

2935 35. There is no inconvenience whatsoever in that, whether by sentence of a universal Council or by
made of all peoples, the Supreme Pontificate be transferred from the bishop and the city of

2936 36. A definition of a national Council does not admit further discussion and the civil power

2937 37. National churches may be established that are subtracted and totally separated from the

2938 38. The excessive arbitrariness of the Roman Pontiffs contributed to the division

Church

S VIII. Errors about Christian marriage

2965 65. It cannot be demonstrated for any reason that Christ elevated marriage to dignity

others by the doctrine proposed and affirmed, which all Catholics must maintain

S X. Errors related to current liberalism

2977 77. In our age it is no longer appropriate for the Catholic religion to be considered the only one

Dogmatic Constitution 1 on the Church of Christ

3050 [Of the institution and foundation of the Church.] The eternal Shepherd and guardian of our
souls [1 Petr. 2, 25], to make the salutary work of redemption perennial, he decreed to build
the Holy Church in which, as in the house of the living God, all the faithful were united by the
bond of a single faith and charity. Therefore, before he was glorified, he prayed to the Father, not only

for the Apostles, but also for all those who were to believe in Him through the word
of those, so that they would all be one, just as the same Son and the Father are
just one thing [loh. 17, 20s]. Now, in the manner in which he sent the Apostles—whom
had chosen out of the world—as He Himself had been sent by the Father [Ioh. 20, 21]; so
He wanted there to be pastors and doctors in his Church until the end of the ages [Mt. 28,
20]. 3051 But so that the episcopate itself would be one and undivided and the universal multitude
of believers to be preserved in the unity of faith and communion through the priests
consistent with each other; By putting the blessed Peter before the other Apostles, he instituted in him
a perpetual principle of one and another unity and a visible foundation, on the strength of which
build an eternal temple, and the height of the Church, which was to reach heaven, would rise
about the firmness of this faith. 3052 and since the gates of hell, to overthrow, if it were
possible, to the Church, rise up everywhere with increasing hatred against its foundation
divinely settled; We judge it to be necessary for the protection, safety and increase of the
Catholic flock, to propose with the approval of the sacred Council, the doctrine on the institution,
perpetuity and nature of the sacred apostolic primacy - in which lies the strength and solidity of
the whole Church—so that it may be believed and maintained by all the faithful, according to the ancient and
constant faith of the universal Church, and at the same time proscribe and condemn contrary errors, in
so much harmful to the flock of the Lord.
